# TCP listener

The `tcp` listener configures Boundary to listen on a TCP address and port. It supports all four listener [purposes](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners#listener-purposes): `api`, `cluster`, `proxy`, and `ops`.

```hcl
listener "tcp" {
  purpose = "api"
  address = "127.0.0.1:9200"
}
```

You can define the `listener` stanza more than once to make Boundary listen on multiple interfaces. A controller requires exactly one listener with the `cluster` purpose. Refer to [Configure multiple listeners](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/configure-multiple-listeners) for examples.

## Custom response headers

Boundary supports defining custom HTTP response headers for responses returned by controller `api` listeners. You define headers by the HTTP status code of the response. For example, you can define one list of headers for `200` responses and another for `307` responses.

You can also define headers for hundred-level status codes. Headers defined for `4xx` apply to `400`, `401`, `404`, and all other 400-level responses.

Boundary applies headers in order of specificity. A header defined for a specific status code overrides the same header at the hundred-level, which overrides the `default` value. To remove a header at a specific level, define it with an empty list.

Two parameters define custom response headers on a TCP `api` listener:

- `custom_api_response_headers` applies to API endpoint responses, which are all paths that start with `/v1/`.
- `custom_ui_response_headers` applies to all other paths. Use this parameter to set headers for content served to a web browser, such as `Content-Security-Policy`.

Boundary requires `script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in the UI content security policy to support session recording playback. Keep that value if you override `Content-Security-Policy` for UI requests.

Refer to [Configure custom response headers](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/configure-custom-response-headers) for step-by-step instructions and examples.
